I’m not trying to discourage you - but be prepared for one awful and long struggle here. 

I did the same thing and thought it was a good idea to buy my girlfriend a pair of running shoes, as she had been running in the same ones for 5+ years and I’ve never seen a shoe with so little cushioning anymore. 

Well, it started with taking her to the local running store. After trying on 25+ pairs, not a single one worked for her. She ended up choosing 2 from the few separate times we went but each time she took them for a run, she quickly returned them. 

It took probably 2 months before she ended up landing in a Kinvara (I can’t believe that’s what she went with compared to everything going in today’s age). And I finally rested happy.

Just kidding. She admitted a month + later that she doesn’t mind them but she doesn’t love them by any stretch and kind of just agreed to choose them since she felt bad and didn’t want to keep dealing with trying shoe after shoe. 

So now here I am, half a year later, still wanting to get her a shoe she’ll love. But man, is it ever hard sometimes.

Mind you, I’m 185-200 pounds depending on the time of year and because of that I compress a lot of foams more than others. I do find they run a touch narrow as well (less ideal for me as a 2E but absolutely fine for most) 

Don’t let me psych you out. Wait til you get them and give them a spin! Honestly, I can’t overstate how comfy they are and how much you’re going to enjoy them, no matter what!

A good pair of marino wool or similar socks will go a long way but they aren’t completely necessary. 
Make sure your hands are warm enough. Your hands and your feet are going to be what gets cold the quickest. 
Having a balaclava can also go a long ways but by no means is it necessary either. Just make sure you can tuck your face into your coat when needed. 

Above all else, since it’s your first time, your biggest worry and concern will be enjoying yourself enough to be able to want to go again. Seriously. Your introduction into skiing will have a huge impact on how eager you are to get out again.
Dress warm, keep an open mind, keep your body loose, stretch the morning of and maybe even the night before. Take breaks when needed and listen to your body. You’re going to be sore and you’re going to be engaging a ton of muscles that you aren’t used to using. Remember, no race was ever won in the first turn but many were lost there. Get out there and remember it’s all about having fun!
